HexGo Edge Eyes: rule examples

31 worked examples of what is captured, what is safe and what is illegal, on a board of 5 per side unless stated. Each outcome was written down from the rules and then played on the engine and on the independent reference engine.

All 124 checks agree with both engines. A ✓ means the engines do what the line says; it does not mean the rule itself is what you want.

Reading the diagrams. The thick outline is the board edge. A dashed circle is a move about to be played, in the mover’s colour, lettered or numbered. In the “After” diagrams the stone just played carries its label and a red ✕ marks each captured stone. Cells are named by row letter and position in the row.

1. Liberty pairs

A group stays on the board while it has a liberty pair: two empty cells that touch each other and both touch the group. Counting liberties is not enough; two liberties that do not touch each other do not save a group.

1.1 A lone stone, opponent on every other side

Three liberties, none of them touching another, is not a liberty pair.

  • ✓ a · White F4: legal, captures 1. Black is left with three liberties that are all apart from each other.

1.2 Two liberties: touching or not

With two liberties left, the stone lives only if the two liberties touch.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White D4: legal, captures nothing. The two liberties left are next to each other: a liberty pair.
  • ✓ b · White F4: legal, captures 1. The two liberties left are on opposite sides and do not touch.

1.3 The same rule for a group of two

A group is judged as a whole: any two touching empty cells next to any of its stones will do.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E4: legal, captures nothing. Two touching liberties remain below the left stone.
  • ✓ b · White F4: legal, captures 2. Four liberties remain, but no two of them touch.

1.4 Suicide is not allowed

A move that leaves your own group without a liberty pair or two eye cells, and captures nothing, is illegal.

  • ✓ a · White E5: illegal (suicide). White would have three liberties, none touching.

1.5 Captures are settled before suicide

The opponent’s groups are judged first. A move that would be suicide is legal if it captures and the capture gives the mover a liberty pair.

  • ✓ a · White E5: legal, captures 1. The Black stone on the right is left with three liberties that do not touch, so it goes. The cell it leaves gives White a liberty pair.

1.6 No taking straight back (ko)

A move may not recreate an earlier position of the whole board.

Moves are played in order.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures 1. As in the previous example.
  • ✓ 2 · Black E6: illegal (repeats a position). Retaking would capture the White stone and put the board back exactly as it was.

2. Stones on the edge

There is no wrap-around at the edge. A liberty pair is always two empty cells that really touch, so an edge stone (four neighbours) and a corner stone (three) are easier to capture than a stone in the middle.

2.1 Edge stone: captured by two stones

An edge stone’s four neighbours run in a line from edge to edge. It lives only while two of them that sit side by side are empty.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White D7: legal, captures 1. The two liberties left are the neighbours along the edge, on either side of the stone. They do not touch.
  • ✓ b · White D8: legal, captures 1. The two liberties left do not touch.
  • ✓ c · White B6: legal, captures nothing. The two liberties left are side by side: a liberty pair.

2.2 Corner stone: captured by one stone

A corner stone has three neighbours. The middle one touches both of the others, so taking it leaves two liberties that do not touch.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White B5: legal, captures 1. The two liberties left lie along the two edges and do not touch.
  • ✓ b · White B6: legal, captures nothing. The two liberties left are side by side: a liberty pair.

3. Eyes away from the edge

An eye is a connected area of empty cells bordered only by one colour. A group with no liberty pair stays on the board if it borders at least two eye cells in total. An invading stone that cannot live itself does not break the eye. In these examples Black has no liberties outside, so only the eyes matter.

3.1 One one-cell eye is not enough

One eye cell does not save a group. It needs a liberty pair or two eye cells.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E7: legal, captures 6. Black is left with one eye cell and one outside liberty. They do not touch, and one eye cell is not two.
  • ✓ b · White E5: illegal (suicide). Black still has its liberty pair outside, so nothing is captured and the White stone has no liberties.

3.2 Two one-cell eyes: unsafe

Two separate single eyes are exactly two eye cells. Filling either leaves one, and the group is captured.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E4: legal, captures 11. One eye cell is left.
  • ✓ b · White E6: legal, captures 11. One eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

3.3 Three one-cell eyes: safe

Fill one of three single eyes and two eye cells remain, so nothing is captured and the move is suicide.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E3: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White E5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White E7: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.4 One two-cell eye: unsafe

An invader that cannot live does not break the eye, but the cell it stands on no longer counts. One eye cell is left.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E5: legal, captures 8. One empty eye cell is left.
  • ✓ b · White E6: legal, captures 8. One empty eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

3.5 A two-cell eye and a one-cell eye: safe

Three eye cells in total: whichever one White takes, two remain.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E3: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White E5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White E6: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.6 Straight three: safe

A stone inside has at most two liberties and they do not touch, so it cannot live, and two eye cells remain.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E4: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White E5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White E6: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.7 Bent three: safe

Same as the straight three: the two end cells do not touch each other.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White F5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White F6: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.8 Triangle of three: unsafe (White plays twice)

In a triangle the two cells left after an invasion touch each other, so the invader has a liberty pair and lives. A living invader breaks the eye.

Moves are played in order. Black passes in between.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures nothing. White has a liberty pair. So does Black, sharing the same two cells.
  • ✓ 2 · White E6: legal, captures 9. White’s two stones cannot live, so they do not count against the eye, but only one empty eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

3.9 Triangle of three: unsafe (Black answers)

Capturing the invader does not help: it leaves a two-cell eye.

Moves are played in order.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures nothing. White has a liberty pair.
  • ✓ 2 · Black E6: legal, captures 1. The White stone has one liberty left and is captured.
  • ✓ 3 · White E5: legal, captures 10. A two-cell eye: one empty eye cell is left.

3.10 Triangle and a one-cell eye: safe

White can put one stone in the triangle but can never fill it: the last empty triangle cell and the single eye are two eye cells.

Moves are played in order. Black passes throughout.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures nothing. White has a liberty pair. Black shares it.
  • ✓ 2 · White E6: illegal (suicide). White’s two stones cannot live; one triangle cell plus the single eye is two eye cells.
  • ✓ 3 · White E3: illegal (suicide). Black still has the liberty pair in the triangle.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.11 Two two-cell eyes: safe

Four eye cells: an invader takes one and three remain.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E3: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White F3: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White E6: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ d · White D5: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.12 Straight four: safe

No stone inside a straight line can get a liberty pair.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White E3: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White E4: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White E5: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.
  • ✓ d · White E6: illegal (suicide). Three eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

3.13 Diamond of four: unsafe if Black ignores it

In a diamond an invader in the middle has a liberty pair. Three White moves in a row capture.

Moves are played in order. Black passes in between.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures nothing. White has a liberty pair.
  • ✓ 2 · White D5: legal, captures nothing. White’s two stones still have a liberty pair (the last two cells touch).
  • ✓ 3 · White E6: legal, captures 10. One empty eye cell is left.

✓ Safe only if Black answers: White captures with free moves, but not if Black replies.

3.14 Diamond of four: safe if Black answers

Black takes the other middle cell, capturing the invader and leaving a bent three.

Moves are played in order.

  • ✓ 1 · White E5: legal, captures nothing. White has a liberty pair.
  • ✓ 2 · Black E6: legal, captures 1. The White stone’s two liberties no longer touch.
  • ✓ 3 · White E5: illegal (suicide). The eye is now a bent three.

4. Eyes on the edge

An area closed off by your stones and the board edge is an eye, exactly like one ringed by stones. The same shapes are safe and unsafe as away from the edge.

4.1 Two one-cell eyes on the edge: unsafe

Edge cells closed off by Black are eyes, so this group stands with two eye cells. As away from the edge, two single eyes are one move from capture.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White I2: legal, captures 7. One eye cell is left.
  • ✓ b · White I4: legal, captures 7. One eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

4.2 Three one-cell eyes on the edge, two in corners: safe

Corner cells and edge cells are eyes like any other.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White I1: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White I3: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White I5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

4.3 A two-cell and a one-cell eye on the edge: safe

The position that prompted this rule set. Black’s eyes are F8 (one cell) and H6 + I5 (two cells), all closed off by Black stones and the edge.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White H6: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White I5: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White F8: illegal (suicide). Two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

4.4 Straight three flat along the edge: safe

A stone in the middle cell has a liberty on each side along the edge, but they do not touch each other, so it cannot live.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White I3: illegal (suicide). Two liberties that do not touch; two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White I2: illegal (suicide). One liberty; two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White I4: illegal (suicide). One liberty; two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

4.5 The same stone out in the open

The same edge cell with the same two Black stones above it, but no eye round it. The answer is the same, because the edge never gives a liberty pair.

  • ✓ a · White I3: illegal (suicide). Two liberties along the edge that do not touch, and nothing is captured.

4.6 Two-cell eye flat along the edge: unsafe

Same as a two-cell eye away from the edge.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White I2: legal, captures 5. One empty eye cell is left.
  • ✓ b · White I3: legal, captures 5. One empty eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

4.7 Three cells round a corner: safe

The corner cell’s two neighbours along the edges do not touch each other, so this is a bent three.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White I5: illegal (suicide). Two liberties that do not touch; two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ b · White I4: illegal (suicide). One liberty; two eye cells remain.
  • ✓ c · White H6: illegal (suicide). One liberty; two eye cells remain.

✓ Safe: White cannot capture the group even if Black never answers.

4.8 Triangle on the edge: unsafe

Same as a triangle away from the edge: the invader gets a liberty pair, two cells that really touch.

Moves are played in order. Black passes in between.

  • ✓ 1 · White H4: legal, captures nothing. The two edge cells touch each other: a liberty pair.
  • ✓ 2 · White I3: legal, captures 6. One empty eye cell is left.

✓ Unsafe: White captures the group even if Black replies.

5. Order of events

After a stone is placed, the opponent’s groups are judged first and captured; only then are the mover’s own groups judged.

5.1 Two groups sharing their only liberty pair

White’s wall and the four Black stones inside it share one liberty pair, D3 and E2. Whoever fills it leaves both groups without a pair, but the opponent is judged first, so the mover captures.

Each lettered move is tried separately from the position shown.

  • ✓ a · White D3: legal, captures 4. Black’s four stones are judged first and captured; that gives White’s wall its liberties back.
  • ✓ b · White E2: legal, captures 4. Black’s four stones are judged first and captured; that gives White’s wall its liberties back.
